# Implementation Plan: Additive opt-in LAN known-devices remote-session transport
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"remote-connectivity-lan-known-devices-additive-transport"} -->


*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-26 (from brainstorm `remote-connectivity-lan-known-devices-additive-transport`). Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/remote-connectivity-lan-known-devices-additive-transport/plan.md`.*

## Overview

Add an **opt-in, default-off LAN remote-session transport** to codexu's embedded per-daemon happy-server, **alongside** Microsoft Dev Tunnels (which stays the default and byte-for-byte unchanged). The motivation: the operator's corporate policy blocks Dev Tunnels, so the remote-session feature (Android e-ink BOOX tablet ↔ dev box) is unusable. Same-LAN reachability on the corp Wi-Fi is operator-confirmed working (2026-06-27), and the Cloudflare provider-swap alternative (D-002) is ruled out (the central `happy.evyatar.dev` server/tunnel is retired; the architecture is distributed per-daemon).

The single load-bearing constraint: the embedded happy-server tunnel listener has **zero per-request auth** — it relies entirely on the Dev Tunnels gateway for authentication and a loopback bind for confinement (`assertOperatorIdentityGate`). A naive LAN bind keeps reachability and deletes the trust root; `POST /pair/complete` is unauthenticated and lets any LAN host self-enroll. Therefore the "known devices" allowlist is implemented as a **NEW fail-closed, server-side, per-request cryptographic auth mode** (`auth: 'lan'`) enforced as a single global hook covering every HTTP route AND the Socket.IO handshake, reusing the existing Ed25519/X25519 TOFU key material and the `agentComms/peerAuth` pinned-key/sealed-body machinery. IP/host/mDNS allowlists are explicitly NO-GO as the security boundary. The codex side gates the feature behind a new experimental `Feature` variant (default off) and surfaces it via `/remote on`.

## Approach

### Architecture

A new happy-server `auth: 'lan'` mode whose listener does not bind non-loopback until a **live per-request cryptographic device verifier** is active. The verifier is a single shared core (`lanDeviceAuth.ts`) attached as ONE global Fastify hook that fires on **every** registered route — including the bare `GET /` welcome (`api.ts:66`), the `enableMonitoring` `GET /health` liveness route (which runs a `SELECT 1` DB query and registers its own `onRequest` hook at `enableMonitoring.ts:8`), and `GET /files/*` — closing the `/pair/complete` no-preHandler gap, with an explicit, default-empty public-path allowlist and a stated ordering relative to the `enableMonitoring` hook. **Fastify hook-phase caveat:** `onRequest` fires BEFORE body parsing, so the body-hash portion of the signature cannot be computed there — body-dependent verification must run at `preValidation`/`preHandler` (where the parsed body is available) or capture the raw body; the design splits the hook accordingly. The **same verifier instance** also drives a `'lan'` branch in the Socket.IO `createSocketAuthMiddleware`, so the HTTP and socket planes cannot diverge. The mechanism is **per-device Ed25519 signed-request** (canonical signature over a fully-specified form: exact signed headers + canonical path/query + body-hash + timestamp + nonce, with a short replay window) reusing the TOFU key material and the **pattern** (not a cross-package import) of the `agentComms/peerAuth`/`ingestHandler` pinned-key/sealed-body machinery — the verifier lives in happy-server (which already depends on `@noble/ed25519`, `@noble/hashes`, `privacy-kit`, and `tweetnacl`) or a shared `happy-wire` module, NOT imported from happy-cli internals. A server-side known-device allowlist (a pinned-pubkey store mirroring `peerAuth`'s `peers.json` + fingerprint-change rejection) holds the blessed device pubkeys and is the revocation surface, exposed via dedicated LAN-gated device-list/revoke server routes. Enrollment is gated out-of-band (one-time daemon-minted/displayed QR/PIN secret with a defined expiry) since there is no gateway on LAN — **no LAN self-enrollment**.

On the transport side, a `LanDaemonProvider` implements the existing `DaemonTunnelProvider` interface and advertises the LAN `http://<lan-ip>:<port>` address. Provider selection in `daemon/run.ts:210-211` becomes conditional on a **happy-cli daemon-side opt-in** — a persisted/env/CLI setting (e.g. `HAPPY_LAN_TRANSPORT=1` or a `machine.json`/account-settings flag) read by the daemon BEFORE `dualListenerBinding()`. This is a **distinct layer** from the codex `Feature` gate: the Rust Feature flag governs whether codex's `/remote on` offers/selects LAN, but it cannot by itself change the Node daemon's startup; the daemon opt-in is what actually swaps the provider and bind. New LAN request/handshake headers must also be added to the hard-coded CORS/socket `allowedHeaders` (`api.ts:61-64`, `socket.ts:105`) or browser/desktop preflight will strip them. The recommended listener model is **Option B (single selected remote listener: Dev Tunnels by default, LAN replaces the tunnel listener when opted in)** so there is only ever one non-loopback listener and the "non-loopback ⇒ verifier active" invariant holds with no concurrent unauthenticated peer (see Open Questions to confirm vs. a concurrent third listener).

The app learns the LAN endpoint via a manual URL / QR (reachability only; mDNS is a future non-security convenience), generates and stores its own Ed25519 device keypair (greenfield), registers via the gated enrollment, attaches the device-proof header on HTTP and the socket handshake through transport-specific builders, and exposes an opt-in Settings toggle plus a known-devices revoke UI. The codex side adds an experimental `Feature` variant (default off) and threads the LAN transport choice through the existing `/remote on` onboard/cancel state machine.

### Implementation Strategy

Ordered by the dependency spine (each forces the next), front-loading the property that makes or breaks safety (one fail-closed verifier covering every route + the socket handshake):

1. **Preflight** (US-001): confirm happy-server honors a non-loopback bind and the LAN port is reachable on the corp Wi-Fi; define the NO-GO criteria. Cheapest disconfirming check before the XL build.
2. **Server contract + verifier core** (US-002): `auth: 'lan'` union + `lanDeviceAuth.ts` verifier + known-device allowlist/revocation store + enrollment-bootstrap design. The wire/key contract everything binds to — lands first.
3. **Server enforcement wiring** (US-003): relax `assertOperatorIdentityGate` (fail-closed), register the global verifier hook on every route at the body-aware Fastify phase (`preValidation`/`preHandler`) + the socket `'lan'` branch, gate `/pair/complete` enrollment, add LAN CORS/socket `allowedHeaders`, update the `.d.ts` mirror, and record the relaxed-bind sign-off.
4. **Server hostile-client + non-crossing-auth test suite** (US-004): the decisive acceptance gate.
5. **happy-cli transport** (US-005): `LanDaemonProvider` + provider selection + `dualListenerBinding` change + `machine.json` migration + bind/port validation. Parallel-safe with the app work.
6. **happy-app LAN client** (US-006): device-keypair, LAN endpoint learning, device-proof attach, gated enrollment. Parallel-safe with cli.
7. **happy-app Settings opt-in + revoke UI + i18n** (US-007): after the client.
8. **codex Feature gate + `/remote on` LAN** (US-008): after the cli transport exists to gate.
9. **Docs + invariant sign-off** (US-009): `docs/security-model.md` + `AGENTS.md` amendment, last.

## Scope

### In Scope
- A new happy-server `auth: 'lan'` mode that permits a non-loopback bind only when a live per-request cryptographic verifier is active, enforced fail-closed across every HTTP route (`/pair/complete`, `/pair/connect`, `/files/*`, both-listener routes, all tunnel-only routes) and the Socket.IO handshake.
- A `lanDeviceAuth.ts` verifier core (per-device Ed25519 signed-request + nonce/timestamp replay window) reusing TOFU key material + the `agentComms/peerAuth`/`ingestHandler` PATTERN (re-implemented in happy-server via its own `@noble`/`tweetnacl` deps, NOT imported from happy-cli), plus a server-side known-device allowlist/revocation store with LAN-gated device-list/revoke routes and an out-of-band (QR/PIN) enrollment gate.
- A `LanDaemonProvider` on the existing `DaemonTunnelProvider` seam, provider selection behind a happy-cli daemon opt-in (env/config/CLI, distinct from the codex Feature gate), `dualListenerBinding` wiring (Option B default), `machine.json` LAN field migration, and the daemon-side QR/PIN enrollment-secret mint.
- happy-app: device-keypair generation/storage, LAN endpoint learning (manual URL/QR), device-proof attachment (HTTP + socket), gated enrollment, a default-off Settings opt-in toggle, and a known-LAN-devices revoke UI (with i18n in all locales).
- codex: a new experimental `Feature` variant (default off) gating the LAN variant, threaded through `/remote on` (incl. cancellation) and `daemon_supervisor`.
- Docs: `docs/security-model.md` + `packages/happy-cli/AGENTS.md` amendment recording the reviewed, gated happy-server LAN exception with formal sign-off.

### Out of Scope
- Any change to the default Dev Tunnels behavior, the loopback listener, codex-happy's same-machine loopback attach, or the **codex app-server WS transport** loopback-only invariant (`packages/happy-cli/AGENTS.md` `## Codex Transport Security Model`).
- An IP allowlist, host allowlist, or mDNS-name trust used AS the security boundary (NO-GO). mDNS may exist only as future non-security discovery convenience.
- D-002 (Cloudflare provider-swap, ruled out) and D-003 (WireGuard mesh, fallback only).
- A multi-tenant / central happy-server (architecture is one embedded server per daemon).
- Bounded-plaintext-memory or other unrelated refactors of the touched files.

## Risk Areas
- **A subtly-wrong signature/enrollment check is a WORSE open door than Dev Tunnels because it looks secure.** Mitigation: the global-hook design (one place, completeness verified by enumerating against `api.ts:104-117`), the same verifier instance for HTTP + socket, fail-closed gate semantics, and the mandatory hostile-client suite (US-004).
- **Enrollment chicken-and-egg:** `/pair/complete` establishes the shared secret it would need to authenticate; on LAN there is no gateway. Resolved by an out-of-band one-time QR/PIN enrollment secret (no self-enrollment). Get the design reviewed before US-006.
- **Route-coverage gap:** one missed route = total bypass. The global hook must cover routes registered OUTSIDE `api.ts:104-117` too — the bare `GET /` (`api.ts:66`) and `enableMonitoring`'s `GET /health` (`SELECT 1`, its own `onRequest` at `enableMonitoring.ts:8`). The structural guard is "the LAN hook fires on every registered route" + an explicit, default-empty public-path allowlist, with the LAN hook's ordering relative to `enableMonitoring`'s hook stated; completeness is verified against the live Fastify route table, not a hand-maintained list.
- **Fastify hook phasing:** body-hash signing cannot run in `onRequest` (pre-body-parse); use `preValidation`/`preHandler` or raw-body capture, and add the LAN signature header to CORS/socket `allowedHeaders` or preflight strips it.
- **`machine.json` migration** touches every reader/writer; do it atomically. **`tokenStorage.ts`** filters old pinned-key shapes — the LAN device key must not be stripped.
- **DHCP IP churn** breaks the stored LAN URL (not the trust — the pin is to the device key); re-discovery (new QR / manual re-entry) re-binds the URL.
- **Cross-package wire contract** (auth union + device-proof schema) spans happy-server/happy-cli/happy-app (+ possibly happy-wire); Zod strips unmirrored fields — mirror all copies.
- **codex overlay rebase surface:** keep the upstream edit minimal (enum + spec), put logic in the overlay, and coordinate with the recently-shipped autoconnect/self-onboard/cancellation work in `remote_on.rs`.
- **Relaxing a written security invariant** requires formal sign-off + docs update (US-009), and the gate error string must describe the carve-out rather than be silently weakened.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dev Tunnels remains the default and works unchanged — verified concretely: the default provider stays `DevTunnelsDaemonProvider` (`run.ts:210-211`, LAN opt-in absent), the default bind stays `127.0.0.1`, and the existing pairing/socket/dual-listener tests pass byte-for-byte. LAN is opt-in and default-off (codex Feature flag off by default; happy-cli daemon opt-in absent by default; app toggle default off). Existing happy-server / happy-cli / happy-app test suites pass.
- The LAN listener does NOT bind any non-loopback interface unless the per-request cryptographic verifier is active; `assertOperatorIdentityGate` still throws on a bare non-loopback bind without the verifier (covered by a unit test).
- **Signature canonicalization is fully specified and tested:** the exact signed headers, canonical path+query handling, body-hash, timestamp-skew window, nonce store + lifetime, and the socket-handshake canonical form are pinned; an expired/replayed/forged signature fails closed (automated tests for each).
- **Hostile-client acceptance (decisive):** an unpaired/unblessed client that can reach the LAN listener is fail-closed rejected on EVERY reachable entry point — the bare `GET /` welcome (`api.ts:66`), the `enableMonitoring` `GET /health` route (runs `SELECT 1`), `/files/*`, `/pair/complete`, `/pair/connect`, `accountRoutes`/`machineSelfRoutes`, every tunnel-only HTTP route, the device-list/revoke routes, AND the Socket.IO `/v1/updates` handshake — it cannot self-enroll, create a session, probe liveness/DB, enumerate version/dev routes, or trigger any handler. The completeness anchor is "every Fastify route the listener registers (including `enableMonitoring` + the bare `/`)", verified by enumerating the live route table, not just `api.ts:104-117`. Proven by an automated test (forged/absent signature ⇒ 401/handshake-reject on every entry point); any intentionally-public path is on an explicit justified allowlist (default: none).
- The dual-listener non-crossing-auth invariant holds: a loopback capability never satisfies the LAN plane and a LAN proof never satisfies the loopback plane (automated test).
- A blessed client (pinned Ed25519 key, valid signed request within the replay window) completes a remote session against a LAN-bound listener with Dev Tunnels disabled — proven by an AUTOMATED integration test using a second in-process/loopback client (the autonomously-verifiable form), with the physical BOOX-over-Wi-Fi run recorded as manual evidence (not a CI gate). Revoking the device via the device-revoke route/Settings UI causes the verifier to fail closed on that device's next request AND socket handshake (automated test).
- The codex app-server WS transport invariant (`AGENTS.md` `## Codex Transport Security Model`) is unchanged; the reviewed decision to relax the happy-server bind invariant is recorded WITH the server-contract change (US-003), and `docs/security-model.md` + `AGENTS.md` carry the full carve-out write-up (US-009). The sign-off artifact is the `docs/security-model.md §Operator Identity Gate` amendment plus explicit operator approval of the relaxed-bind decision.
- Per-package typecheck/tests green: `pnpm --filter happy-server build`, `pnpm --filter happy build` (+ `vitest run`), `pnpm --filter happy-app typecheck`; codex `cargo check --workspace` + `cargo test -p codex-happy`; happy-app `translations.test.ts` passes with new keys in all locales.

## Open Questions
- **Listener concurrency (Option A vs B):** recommended Option B (Dev Tunnels XOR LAN, single remote listener) for the simpler "non-loopback ⇒ verifier active" invariant; confirm vs. a concurrent third listener (which keeps Dev Tunnels live alongside LAN at a wider attack surface). [Decide in US-002.]
- **Enrollment gate mechanism:** one-time daemon-displayed QR vs. numeric PIN vs. operator-confirm-on-daemon for the first `/pair/complete`. Recommended QR (matches existing pairing UX); confirm BOOX e-ink QR scanning is acceptable.
- **Signature canonicalization details:** exact replay window length, nonce store (in-memory vs. sibling JSON), and whether to additionally seal bodies (reuse `openSealedBody`) or only sign. Recommended: sign method+path+body-hash+timestamp+nonce with a short window; settle in US-002.
- **Transport schema shape (RESOLVED → US-002):** both `packages/happy-cli/src/tunnel/types.ts` and `packages/happy-wire/src/tunnel/types.ts` require Dev-Tunnels-shaped fields (`tunnelId`/`tunnelName`/`tags`/`owner`) that LAN lacks. US-002 introduces a discriminated `transport: 'dev-tunnels' | 'lan'` variant (or makes the Dev-Tunnels-only fields optional) in both packages; not deferrable because US-006 binds to the wire shape.
- **HMAC-over-`mobileSharedSecret` fallback:** only if Ed25519 signed-request proves infeasible on the BOOX; documented as the lower-tier fallback.
- **`[INFERRED]` autonomous-mode defaults** above (mechanism = Ed25519 signed-request, listener = Option B, enrollment = QR) are recommendations grounded in the research, not operator-confirmed; the impl member should surface them for confirmation if cheap, else proceed and document.
